rows.description: A toddler in a loud, crowded wedding or market may cover ears, cry, cling or shut down. The child has too much sensory input to cope and needs a quieter space and a familiar adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child in stifling heat becomes irritable, tearful and quick to hit, and may not know why. Cool water, shade and rest often change behaviour faster than correction.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teacher sees children becoming louder, more restless and quarrelsome in a hot, crowded room. Fresh air, water breaks and quieter moments matter for behaviour as much as rules do.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a small, busy house with constant noise and no private corner may feel constantly irritated and unable to think. Even a small personal spot and agreed quiet times can ease tension.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult packed into a hot bus or train feels sweat, pressure and a short fuse, and may snap at a stranger. Recognising the effect of heat and crowding helps to let small provocations pass.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person working in a hot, noisy environment finds concentration falling and irritability rising. Breaks, water, ear protection where possible and postponing big decisions are sensible responses.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Some people, including many with sensory sensitivities, find crowds, bright lights and noise truly painful. Family and colleagues who allow quiet breaks and exit plans make gatherings possible, not a test of character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult on night shifts fights the body clock, feeling foggy, low and out of step with family life. Consistent sleep hours in a dark room and honesty with family about the schedule help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A student flying across many time zones feels sleepy at odd hours, forgetful and irritable for days. Gentle daylight at local times and patience with the body help it adjust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.description: A worker with changing shifts finds sleep, meals and mood constantly disrupted, with increasing exhaustion and short temper. Predictable patterns where possible and health check-ups protect long-term wellbeing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
